newsitem.title: UK: UK to proceed with sales of student loan debt.
newsitem.headline: UK to proceed with sales of student loan debt.

text.p: The new Labour government said on Thursday it would go ahead with plans drawn up by the previous Conservative administration to make substantial sales of student loan debt to the private sector.
Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown said Labour had inherited tough public spending plans that counted on selling its portfolio of student loans, estimated at two billion stg.

"Given the tightness of our plans generally and in particular the priority we want to give to education programmes, the government has decided to proceed with the sale," Brown said in a written parliamentary answer.
He accepted that the government would have to provide continuing subsidies to purchasers of the debt and said the size of them could not be predicted in advance.
Brown said the sales, which will be put out to competitive tender, will enable the private sector to understand student loans better.
This in turn could encourage financial institutions in future to play a more direct role in the provision of student support, he said.
